config.title: Database operations

intro.title: Database operations
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple application that performs basic database operations, such as creating, reading, updating, and deleting data. You will learn the core concept of interacting with a database using structured queries to manage persistent data. The main technologies involved include a database system (like SQLite) and a programming interface (such as a database driver or ORM) to execute operations. By the end, you'll understand how to connect to a database, run queries, and handle data securely and efficiently.
intro.usecase: Database operations are fundamental to virtually every production application that stores and retrieves data. In e-commerce platforms, these operations power product catalogs, shopping carts, and order histories. Content management systems rely on them for creating, updating, and displaying articles or user profiles. Even simple features like user authentication or saving application preferences involve executing queries to read from and write to databases.

objectives: Initialize a database connection with appropriate configuration parameters.
Construct SQL queries to perform CRUD operations on a database table.
Implement error handling for common database operation failures.
Integrate database operations into a simple application workflow.
Configure a connection pool to manage multiple database connections efficiently.
Manipulate data by applying filtering and sorting in database queries.
Bind application variables to SQL query parameters to prevent injection attacks.

steps.title: Import the database client library
steps.instruction: Import the database client library that will be used for all database operations in this lesson.
steps.hint: Add an import statement at the top of your file to bring in the database client library.

// Similar: importing a library for network operations
import axios from 'axios';

steps.hint: Define an object with key-value pairs for the connection parameters. Use appropriate string values for host, username, and password, and a number for port.

successCriteria: The 'dbConfig' object exists and contains the required properties with appropriate values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Create database connection function
steps.instruction: Define a function named 'connectToDatabase' that uses the configuration object to establish and return a database connection.
steps.hint: Create a function that takes no parameters and returns a connection object. Inside the function, use the configuration values to create the connection.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'connectToDatabase' is created that will handle database connections.
successCriteria: The 'connectToDatabase' function is defined and returns a connection object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the function, but make sure it's named 'connectToDatabase' and returns a connection object.

successCriteria: The insertData function is defined with parameters and includes an INSERT query execution.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition is missing or incorrect. Create a function named insertData that handles database insertion.

successCriteria: The queryData function is defined with parameters and returns a SELECT query result.

steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the query handler, but make sure it accepts parameters and returns a SELECT query result.

steps.title: Create error handling wrapper
steps.instruction: Create a wrapper function named 'withErrorHandling' that takes a database operation function as a parameter and returns a new function that catches and handles errors.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts a function parameter, wraps its execution in a try-catch block, and returns either the result or an error object.
steps.expectedOutcome: A wrapper function that can be used to make database operations more robust by catching errors and returning consistent error responses.
successCriteria: The 'withErrorHandling' function is defined, accepts a function parameter, uses try-catch to handle errors, and returns a wrapped function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your wrapper function accepts a function parameter and returns a new function that catches errors.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error handling wrapper isn't quite right. Remember to create a function that wraps other functions with try-catch error handling.

steps.hint: Define a function that returns a pool object configured with your database connection settings.

successCriteria: The setupConnectionPool function is defined and returns a connection pool object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started implementing connection pooling, but make sure your function returns a properly configured pool object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The connection pooling setup isn't implemented correctly. Create a function named setupConnectionPool that configures connection pooling.

steps.hint: Use the export keyword before each function and configuration object to make them available for import in other files.
steps.expectedOutcome: All database operations and configuration are exported as a cohesive module that can be imported elsewhere.
successCriteria: All database functions and configuration are exported using export statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've exported some items, but make sure to export all database functions and configuration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The module exports are incomplete or missing. Check that you've exported all functions and configuration.
